1.explanation:
The React demo (`App.jsx`) shows how to render three different sizes of NumberInput with `readOnly` set. You’ll see the lack of visual change: no `readonly` attribute, no disabled controls, and no read-only CSS class.

The Storybook story (`NumberInput.stories.js`) wires up the `readOnly` prop as a boolean control for easy play in the docs site. It also provides a default story that users can copy directly.

Finally, the RTL test (`NumberInput-readonly.test.js`) asserts that when you pass `readOnly`:

1. The native `<input>` has the `readonly` attribute
2. The input has the expected read-only modifier class
3. Both increment/decrement buttons are disabled and get a modifier class

Use these snippets to verify the missing behavior, then implement the prop in your component and re-run the demos/tests to confirm the bug is fixed.
1.bug_scenario:
In the current NumberInput component there is no visual or structural change when you pass a `readOnly` prop. According to the design specs (shown in the attached images), a read-only NumberInput should:

• Render the native `readonly` attribute on the `<input>` element
• Add a custom CSS modifier class (e.g. `bx--number__input--readonly`)
• Disable the increment/decrement buttons (so they render in a disabled icon color and have no hover/focus states)
• Use the same sizing, spacing, and typography as the enabled component

Because the `readOnly` prop isn’t wired up, none of these styles or behaviors appear — the input still looks and behaves like an enabled component.
